scenes.title: The group chat has been silent for six hours.
scenes.detail: A rare moment of peace. Or a cry for help?

choices.text: Enjoy the silence. Finally, a thought of my own.
choices.reaction: The phone rests. Somewhere, a notification takes a personal day.

choices.text: Send one excellent meme to my favorite person.
choices.reaction: One meme, one recipient. An extremely exclusive comedy tour.

choices.text: Ask if anyone wants to grab food.
choices.reaction: The chat returns from the dead, asking about dietary restrictions.

choices.text: Start a poll for an unnecessarily ambitious group adventure.
choices.reaction: The poll now includes dates, destinations, and someone’s aunt’s canoe.

scenes.title: Your friend unveils a truly terrible haircut.
scenes.detail: They ask, “Be honest. Do you love it?”

choices.text: Ask how they feel about it first.
choices.reaction: The fringe waits nervously while your friend opens the discussion.

choices.text: Gently suggest one small styling adjustment.
choices.reaction: One strategic hair clip joins the negotiating table.

choices.text: Give a clear, kind answer. They did ask.
choices.reaction: Honesty arrives gently. The fringe has retained legal counsel.

choices.text: Find the one genuinely lovely thing and lead with that.
choices.reaction: The haircut has entered its flattering lighting era.

scenes.title: Your entire weekend just opened up.
scenes.detail: No plans. No obligations. A suspicious amount of freedom.

choices.text: Pick one thing and loosely plan around it.
choices.reaction: One booking, several beautifully unassigned hours. Lunch may audition.

choices.text: Make a little itinerary. Freedom deserves structure.
choices.reaction: Your free time now has a check-in time.

choices.text: Walk outside and see what happens.
choices.reaction: You step outside. The pavement was not expecting this responsibility.

choices.text: Keep a few ideas. Commit to absolutely none.
choices.reaction: Three possible weekends are now competing for absolutely no funding.

scenes.title: You inherit a tiny, slightly haunted café.
scenes.detail: The coffee machine works. The business model does not.

choices.text: Build an entire fictional universe around the resident ghost.
choices.reaction: The ghost has an origin story and concerns about merchandise royalties.

choices.text: Fix the menu, clean the counter, serve good coffee.
choices.reaction: The espresso improves. The ghost still refuses to help with dishes.

choices.text: Keep what people already love and make it better.
choices.reaction: Regulars get better pastries. The ghost keeps its usual table.

choices.text: Imagine a café that turns into a cinema at night.
choices.reaction: The ghost requests a screening. You suspect it means Ghost.

scenes.title: You know exactly one person at this party.
scenes.detail: They have vanished into the kitchen. Naturally.

choices.text: Find the balcony and a good view.
choices.reaction: The skyline makes small talk. Surprisingly, it’s quite good at it.

choices.text: Have a real conversation with whoever is nearest.
choices.reaction: One conversation deep, you’ve learned the dog’s entire medical history.

choices.text: Introduce myself to a small group.
choices.reaction: You join the circle. Someone immediately explains whose kitchen this is.

choices.text: Ask the room a question everyone has an opinion about.
choices.reaction: The room is now passionately litigating the correct way to load dishwashers.

scenes.title: A friend texts: “My day was a disaster.”
scenes.detail: There is no punctuation after disaster. This is serious.

choices.text: Ask if they want comfort or solutions.
choices.reaction: Two help options. Finally, a menu without a QR code.

choices.text: Help separate what happened from what can change.
choices.reaction: The day’s disasters separate into two piles. Neither requires a label maker.

choices.text: Work through a concrete plan for tomorrow.
choices.reaction: Tomorrow gets a plan. Tonight gets to remain in sweatpants.

choices.text: Make them feel heard before anything else.
choices.reaction: The bad day gets a listener. Tomorrow can wait outside.

scenes.title: You leave for a trip in two hours.
scenes.detail: Your bag is empty. Your optimism is not.

choices.text: Run through a short mental checklist.
choices.reaction: Passport, socks, charger. Your brain briefly becomes a departure board.

choices.text: Use the packing list I definitely already have.
choices.reaction: The packing list emerges, presumably wearing its own tiny lanyard.

choices.text: Throw in the essentials. The rest is a local shopping opportunity.
choices.reaction: Your toothbrush is about to become an international purchase.

choices.text: Pack the obvious things and improvise the rest.
choices.reaction: Socks are in. The charger will have to negotiate.

scenes.title: You can take one completely free class.
scenes.detail: No certificate. No career move. Just curiosity.

choices.text: Explore what cities might look like in 100 years.
choices.reaction: Flying buses sound lovely. You still expect them to be late.

choices.text: Cook a meal I can make again tomorrow.
choices.reaction: Tomorrow’s dinner just acquired a qualified instructor.

choices.text: Learn how to fix something around the house.
choices.reaction: That wobbly shelf is about to meet its academic rival.

choices.text: Try experimental storytelling. See where it goes.
choices.reaction: Your opening sentence has already requested an unconventional ending.

scenes.title: Something excellent just happened.
scenes.detail: You got the news. The music swells.

choices.text: Sit with the feeling privately for a while.
choices.reaction: A private victory lap. The kettle provides the standing ovation.

choices.text: Tell my closest person, in great detail.
choices.reaction: Your favorite person gets the news, the context, and the director’s commentary.

choices.text: Tell the group chat. Immediately.
choices.reaction: The group chat receives breaking news and twelve consecutive exclamation marks.

choices.text: Turn it into an impromptu celebration.
choices.reaction: Someone is already searching the drawer for birthday candles.

scenes.title: Your roommate keeps stealing your oat milk.
scenes.detail: The carton has become a symbol.

choices.text: Explain why the small gesture feels inconsiderate.
choices.reaction: The carton is officially about more than breakfast.

choices.text: Agree on a straightforward replacement rule.
choices.reaction: The fridge gets a treaty. Signatures may include a grocery receipt.

choices.text: Split the grocery budget so the system solves it.
choices.reaction: The oat milk has been absorbed into a joint financial venture.

choices.text: Check if something else is going on with them.
choices.reaction: The missing oat milk opens a conversation it was unqualified to host.

scenes.title: The restaurant loses your reservation.
scenes.detail: Eight hungry people look directly at you.

choices.text: Call a nearby alternative before moving everyone.
choices.reaction: The next restaurant receives a very hopeful phone call.

choices.text: Open the backup options I saved earlier.
choices.reaction: Your backup list finally gets the dramatic entrance it deserves.

choices.text: Great. Time for a food adventure.
choices.reaction: The dinner party becomes a walking tour with increasingly audible stomachs.

choices.text: Wander until we find somewhere promising.
choices.reaction: Eight people follow a promising smell. Someone calls it leadership.

scenes.title: How would you describe today?
scenes.detail: One ordinary day. Several possible stories.

choices.text: The beginning of something I cannot quite name yet.
choices.reaction: The title is pending. The opening scene looks promising.

choices.text: The exact small moments that made it good.
choices.reaction: The good coffee makes the highlights reel. It’s visibly proud.

choices.text: What happened, and what I learned from it.
choices.reaction: Today gets a recap. The lesson requests a shorter meeting.

choices.text: The unexpected connections it made me notice.
choices.reaction: Two unrelated moments now share a suspiciously meaningful look.

title: Out of office
subtitle: Meetings that could have been a nap.

scenes.title: The team call starts five minutes early.
scenes.detail: Everyone is awkwardly looking at themselves.

choices.text: Use the five minutes to gather my thoughts.
choices.reaction: Your thoughts assemble while everyone else adjusts their imaginary camera angle.

choices.text: Say hello to the colleague I know best.
choices.reaction: One familiar face. Two people pretending the microphone worked first time.

choices.text: Ask what everyone got up to over the weekend.
choices.reaction: You learn about three hikes and one unexpectedly complicated lasagna.

choices.text: Launch a completely unnecessary icebreaker.
choices.reaction: Someone’s fun fact has just been promoted to opening remarks.

scenes.title: A teammate is attached to an idea that will not work.
scenes.detail: The demo is tomorrow. The idea has a name.

choices.text: Ask what matters most to them about it.
choices.reaction: The idea gets a chance to explain its emotional attachment to existing.

choices.text: Compare the options against the actual requirements.
choices.reaction: The requirements enter the room carrying a very short guest list.

choices.text: Show a small test that clearly demonstrates the issue.
choices.reaction: The tiny test speaks. The idea suddenly needs a glass of water.

choices.text: Acknowledge the effort before discussing a change.
choices.reaction: The effort gets acknowledged. The demo quietly loosens its tie.

scenes.title: Your afternoon meetings are canceled.
scenes.detail: A tiny corporate miracle.

choices.text: Choose the top two priorities and block time.
choices.reaction: Two priorities get window seats. The rest can travel tomorrow.

choices.text: Reorganize the queue and execute the new plan.
choices.reaction: The task queue receives a seating chart and a departure announcement.

choices.text: Follow whichever interesting problem catches my eye.
choices.reaction: An interesting problem waves from a tab you thought you’d closed.

choices.text: Pick something useful and leave room to wander.
choices.reaction: One useful task, with a scenic route available afterward.

scenes.title: You get one day to build anything.
scenes.detail: No roadmap. Just a blank whiteboard.

choices.text: Reimagine the entire product from a different starting point.
choices.reaction: The whiteboard asks whether you mean all of it. You do.

choices.text: Fix the annoying thing everyone hits daily.
choices.reaction: That daily annoyance has no idea today is its last shift.

choices.text: Make an existing workflow noticeably smoother.
choices.reaction: One less click. Somewhere, a tired index finger sends flowers.

choices.text: Prototype an unusual feature people have not asked for yet.
choices.reaction: The prototype exists. Its future users have yet to be informed.

scenes.title: You arrive at the offsite dinner.
scenes.detail: Someone says “networking.” You feel something.

choices.text: Find a quiet seat with a good exit strategy.
choices.reaction: Your seat offers excellent acoustics and direct access to leaving.

choices.text: Have a long conversation with one person.
choices.reaction: The appetizers arrive midway through one surprisingly excellent conversation.

choices.text: Move between a couple of groups.
choices.reaction: You visit two tables. Your bread roll establishes a home base.

choices.text: Make sure every table knows every other table.
choices.reaction: The tables merge socially. Facilities would like everyone to remain seated.

scenes.title: A colleague misses a deadline you relied on.
scenes.detail: The notification arrives with “sorry” three times.

choices.text: Talk through the pressure they are under.
choices.reaction: Three apologies later, the workload finally gets its own speaking part.

choices.text: Figure out the impact and agree a realistic recovery.
choices.reaction: A revised date emerges. The calendar agrees to stop glaring.

choices.text: Identify what failed in the process and fix the dependency.
choices.reaction: The broken handoff gets investigated. The third “sorry” can retire.

choices.text: Check whether they are okay first.
choices.reaction: The deadline waits outside while you check on the actual person.

scenes.title: A launch is moved forward by a week.
scenes.detail: The countdown suddenly has teeth.

choices.text: Cut scope and put the essentials in order.
choices.reaction: The nice-to-haves receive a polite invitation to next month.

choices.text: Map dependencies, owners, and the critical path.
choices.reaction: Every arrow gets an owner. Even the arrows look less worried.

choices.text: Start moving and adapt as the details emerge.
choices.reaction: The launch moves. You move too. The details jog to catch up.

choices.text: Identify a starting point and adjust daily.
choices.reaction: One first step. Tomorrow’s plan can meet you there.

scenes.title: A customer describes a weird workaround.
scenes.detail: It involves three tabs and a sticky note.

choices.text: Sketch an entirely new way to solve the underlying problem.
choices.reaction: The workaround gets a new house instead of another extension.

choices.text: Solve the exact friction they showed us.
choices.reaction: The sticky note submits its retirement notice.

choices.text: Improve the workflow for similar customers.
choices.reaction: Three tabs become fewer tabs. Nobody holds a farewell party.

choices.text: Wonder what hidden need created that behavior.
choices.reaction: You ask why. The sticky note suddenly seems like a witness.

scenes.title: You built something you are proud of.
scenes.detail: There is one slot left in the company demo.

choices.text: Write it up so people can explore at their own pace.
choices.reaction: Your work gets a premiere with optional attendance and excellent headings.

choices.text: Show my immediate team first.
choices.reaction: The team gets a private screening. Someone still asks for the link.

choices.text: Volunteer for a short walkthrough.
choices.reaction: Five minutes, one walkthrough, and a cursor trying to look natural.

choices.text: Take the stage and make it an event.
choices.reaction: The demo has an opening act. It’s your loading animation.

scenes.title: Two teams both need your help first.
scenes.detail: Both messages are marked urgent. Of course.

choices.text: Talk to both leads and understand their worries.
choices.reaction: Two urgent messages become two conversations. Your tea applies for overtime.

choices.text: Compare the consequences of each delay.
choices.reaction: The competing emergencies are asked to bring specific examples.

choices.text: Use impact and effort to make the tradeoff explicit.
choices.reaction: The word “urgent” must now complete the same form as everyone else.

choices.text: Start with the team feeling most unsupported.
choices.reaction: You pull up a chair where the silence sounds particularly overworked.

scenes.title: Someone says “let’s just brainstorm.”
scenes.detail: No agenda. No end time. A dangerous sentence.

choices.text: Agree a question and a time limit first.
choices.reaction: The brainstorm gets an end time. Your lunch visibly relaxes.

choices.text: Define the outcome, constraints, and decision process.
choices.reaction: The whiteboard gets a brief before anyone draws the inevitable cloud.

choices.text: Excellent. Let the ideas collide.
choices.reaction: The whiteboard fills. Someone circles a word purely for emphasis.

choices.text: Start talking and discover the shape as we go.
choices.reaction: The sentence starts walking before anyone checks the destination.

scenes.title: What makes a week feel worthwhile?
scenes.detail: The laptop is closing. Finally.

choices.text: The sense we are building toward something transformative.
choices.reaction: The future looks promising. For now, please let the laptop sleep.

choices.text: Useful work that made someone’s day easier.
choices.reaction: Someone’s day got easier. The laptop closes with a modest little flourish.

choices.text: A concrete improvement I can point to.
choices.reaction: You can point at the improvement. The cursor takes a small bow.

choices.text: A discovery that opened up a new direction.
choices.reaction: One discovery later, Monday has acquired an intriguing new tab.

title: The group chat
subtitle: Your people. All their glorious nonsense.

scenes.title: Someone sends a seven-minute voice note.
scenes.detail: The transcript alone could be a novella.

choices.text: Listen quietly and think before replying.
choices.reaction: The seven-minute note gets a thoughtful audience and an intermission.

choices.text: Send a short, thoughtful answer just to them.
choices.reaction: An entire audio novel receives a very considered postcard.

choices.text: Reply with a voice note of my own.
choices.reaction: The voice-note exchange has officially been renewed for a second season.

choices.text: Call them. We are making this a live episode.
choices.reaction: The recorded monologue becomes a live broadcast. Nobody checks the running time.

scenes.title: Your friend wants to text their ex.
scenes.detail: The draft already has three paragraphs.

choices.text: Help them feel less alone before deciding anything.
choices.reaction: The phone stays nearby. So do you.

choices.text: Talk through what is likely to happen if they send it.
choices.reaction: The send button waits while you preview the possible sequels.

choices.text: Suggest saving the draft and reviewing it tomorrow.
choices.reaction: The draft gets a sleepover in Notes.

choices.text: Ask what feeling they hope the message will resolve.
choices.reaction: The draft has three paragraphs. Your question finds the unwritten fourth.

scenes.title: The group wants a weekend away.
scenes.detail: The chat has 94 messages and zero decisions.

choices.text: Narrow it to two dates and two places.
choices.reaction: The destination shortlist is finally shorter than the group chat.

choices.text: Create a poll, a budget, and a booking deadline.
choices.reaction: The holiday now has a deadline. Someone asks if memes count as votes.

choices.text: I will show up wherever we end up.
choices.reaction: You await coordinates. The group chat continues producing a travel documentary.

choices.text: Suggest a rough direction and keep it flexible.
choices.reaction: A general direction enters the chat. Exact coordinates remain negotiable.

scenes.title: You are picking a birthday gift.
scenes.detail: They insist they do not need anything. Suspicious.

choices.text: Create a whole experience around their imaginary dream life.
choices.reaction: Their imaginary life gets a surprisingly convincing booking confirmation.

choices.text: Get the useful thing they keep borrowing.
choices.reaction: Your borrowed thing finally gets a permanent forwarding address.

choices.text: Upgrade something they use every day.
choices.reaction: Their everyday favorite receives a promotion and wrapping paper.

choices.text: Find something that references a private running joke.
choices.reaction: Nobody else understands the gift. The two of you need a minute.

scenes.title: Friday plans get canceled at the last minute.
scenes.detail: The outfit is already on.

choices.text: Change immediately. This is a gift.
choices.reaction: The outfit’s shift ends early. Sweatpants have been called in.

choices.text: See if one friend wants something quieter.
choices.reaction: One friend gets an invitation with considerably less background noise.

choices.text: Message another group and salvage the night.
choices.reaction: The outfit gets a second audition before the evening closes.

choices.text: Invite people over. The event is now here.
choices.reaction: The venue relocates. Your laundry is hastily reassigned to the bedroom.

scenes.title: Two friends disagree and ask you to pick a side.
scenes.detail: You were just trying to eat your chips.

choices.text: Look for what each person needs underneath the argument.
choices.reaction: The argument reveals two requests hiding inside one very long sentence.

choices.text: Separate the facts from the assumptions.
choices.reaction: The facts sit together. The assumptions insist they know the host.

choices.text: Evaluate each claim fairly, even if it is awkward.
choices.reaction: Your chips are now courtroom snacks. Both sides request additional time.

choices.text: Make sure both feel genuinely listened to.
choices.reaction: Both friends get heard. Your chips remain admirably neutral.

scenes.title: A friend arrives with three extra people.
scenes.detail: Your dinner for four has developed ambitions.

choices.text: Rework portions and seating before we start.
choices.reaction: The portions shrink slightly. The seating chart discovers a previously unknown chair.

choices.text: Quickly coordinate food, seats, and who brings what.
choices.reaction: Everyone gets a job. Even the spare stool has responsibilities.

choices.text: Excellent. This just became a potluck.
choices.reaction: The dinner becomes a potluck before the extra guests remove their coats.

choices.text: Order something extra and squeeze everyone in.
choices.reaction: The delivery order grows. Elbows begin diplomatic talks.

scenes.title: A long walk turns into a long conversation.
scenes.detail: No destination. Just very comfortable shoes.

choices.text: Invent the wildly different lives we could have lived.
choices.reaction: Your alternate selves own a vineyard. Neither has explained the financing.

choices.text: Swap actual stories from our week.
choices.reaction: The week’s stories get fresh air and several unnecessary detours.

choices.text: Notice the neighborhood and what is changing.
choices.reaction: The neighborhood gets reviewed. That new bakery scores suspiciously well.

choices.text: Explore a strange idea neither of us can stop thinking about.
choices.reaction: The strange idea gets stranger. Your step count quietly benefits.

scenes.title: A friend brings someone new to the group.
scenes.detail: They seem lovely. And a little overwhelmed.

choices.text: Give them room to settle in.
choices.reaction: The welcome comes with room to breathe and no surprise icebreaker.

choices.text: Ask one easy question and really listen.
choices.reaction: One easy question later, you know a surprisingly excellent dog fact.

choices.text: Introduce them to people with shared interests.
choices.reaction: Two people discover a shared obsession. You quietly claim the introduction credit.

choices.text: Pull them straight into the fun.
choices.reaction: The newcomer joins the fun. Someone offers an extremely unhelpful rules summary.

scenes.title: Your friend asks whether to quit their job.
scenes.detail: They are tired. You care. The rent still exists.

choices.text: Ask what a better day would actually feel like.
choices.reaction: A better Tuesday gets described. The current Tuesday takes notes.

choices.text: Compare options, savings, and realistic timelines.
choices.reaction: The dream gets a budget. Rent insists on attending.

choices.text: Build a decision framework with the key tradeoffs.
choices.reaction: The big decision gets columns. Snacks remain an unlisted requirement.

choices.text: Explore what the job is doing to their wellbeing.
choices.reaction: The job description steps aside so the person can finish their sentence.

scenes.title: Nobody understands the board game rules.
scenes.detail: The instruction booklet is longer than a lease.

choices.text: Read the basics and try a practice round.
choices.reaction: A practice round begins. Nobody agrees whether the score counts.

choices.text: Understand the rules first so everyone has a fair game.
choices.reaction: Page nine finally explains the tiny wooden sheep.

choices.text: Make up a version and start playing.
choices.reaction: The new rules pass unanimously before anyone knows what they mean.

choices.text: Learn as we go. A little confusion is the fun.
choices.reaction: The first round is sponsored by “wait, can you do that?”

scenes.title: What is your favorite part of an old friendship?
scenes.detail: The years have added lore. So much lore.

choices.text: All the futures we can still imagine together.
choices.reaction: You’re still making future plans with someone who remembers your first haircut.

choices.text: The familiar little rituals that still feel right.
choices.reaction: The old ritual returns. Someone still orders the same fries.

choices.text: Having someone who knows what my real life looks like.
choices.reaction: No backstory needed. They already know which cupboard refuses to close.

choices.text: The way we keep discovering new versions of each other.
choices.reaction: New versions, same friend. Your shared jokes need occasional software updates.
